name: movements-091
prompt:
Create beautiful ORIGINAL FORMA exercise art in a clean modern illustrated fitness manual style. Exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 equal cells, landscape 1536x1024. Each cell white with generous margins; no labels, letters, logos, borders or watermarks. Varied fully clothed adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear with a small lime-green accent. Correct anatomy (two arms, two legs), plausible support and weight-bearing, detailed accurate equipment, subtle shadows. Every cell is an EXACT distinct movement/variation matching its description. Show ONE clear representative working position per cell; do not show duplicate athletes, extra limbs, arrows or overlapping phases. Keep the entire athlete and apparatus inside own cell. Never swap freeweights, benches, grips or variations. Read each guide to choose a physically correct pose. Cell positions are mandatory:
Row 1 column 1: supino. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Colocar a barra em linha reta ao peito e descer ate atingir 90 graus

Row 1 column 2: Supported Split Squat. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Supported split squat performed with stable balance support and controlled depth.

Row 1 column 3: Suspended Fallout. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: Adjust the straps so the handles are at an appropriate height, below waist level. Begin standing and grasping the handles. Lean into the straps, moving to an incline push-up position. This will be your starting position. Keeping your arms straight, lean further into the suspension straps, bringing your body closer to the ground, allowing your shoulders to extend, raising your arms up and over your head. Maintain a neutral spine and keep the rest of your body straight, your shoulders being the only joints allowed to move. Pause during the peak contraction, and then return to the starting position.

Row 1 column 4: Suspended Push-Up. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: Anchor your suspension straps securely to the top of a rack or other object. Leaning into the straps, take a handle in each hand and move into a push-up plank position. You should be as close to parallel to the ground as you can manage with your arms fully extended, maintaining good posture. Maintaining a straight, rigid torso, descend slowly by allowing the elbows to flex. Continue until your elbows break 90 degrees, pausing before you extend to return to the starting position.

Row 2 column 1: Suspended Reverse Crunch. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: Secure a set of suspension straps with the handles hanging about a foot off of the ground. Move yourself into a pushup plank position facing away from the rack. Place your feet into the handles. You should maintain a straight posture, not allowing the hips to sag. This will be your starting position. Begin the movement by flexing the knees and hips, drawing the knees to your torso. As you do so, anteriorly tilt your pelvis, allowing your spine to flex. At the top of the controlled motion, return to the starting position.

Row 2 column 2: Suspended Split Squat. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: Suspend your straps so the handles are 18-30 inches from the floor. Facing away from the setup, place your rear foot into the handle behind you. Keep your head looking forward and your chest up, with your knee slightly bent. This will be your starting position. Descend by flexing the knee and hips, lowering yourself to the ground. Keep your weight on the heel of your foot and maintain your posture throughout the exercise. At the bottom of the movement, reverse the motion, extending through the hip and knee to return to the starting position.

Row 2 column 3: Svend Press. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: Begin in a standing position. Press two lightweight plates together with your hands. Hold the plates together close to your chest to create an isometric contraction in your chest muscles. Your fingers should be pointed forward. This is your starting position. Squeeze the plates between your palms and extend your arms directly out in front of you in a controlled motion. Pause at the top of the motion, and then slowly return to the starting position.

Row 2 column 4: T-Bar Row with Handle. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: Position a bar into a landmine or in a corner to keep it from moving. Load an appropriate weight onto your end. Stand over the bar, and position a Double D row handle around the bar next to the collar. Using your hips and legs, rise to a standing position. Assume a wide stance with your hips back and your chest up. Your arms should be extended. This will be your starting position. Pull the weight to your upper abdomen by retracting the shoulder blades and flexing the elbows. Do not jerk the weight or cheat during the movement. After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

Row 3 column 1: Talons fesses. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Touch your heels to your buttocks, while remaining static or moving

Row 3 column 2: Tate Press. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other. By using your thighs to help you get the dumbbells up, clean the dumbbells one arm at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width. Note: when holding the dumbbells in front of you, make sure your arms are wider than shoulder width apart from each other using a pronated (palms forward) grip. Allow your elbows to point out. This is your starting position. Keeping the upper arms stationary, slowly move the dumbbells in and down in a semi circular motion until they touch the upper chest while inhaling. Keep full control of the dumbbells at all times and do not move the upper arms nor rest the dumbbells on the chest. As you breathe out, move the dumbbells up using your triceps and the same semi-circular motion but in reverse. Attempt to keep the dumbbells together as they move up. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down again slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up. Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

Row 3 column 3: The Straddle. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Begin in a seated, upright position. Start by extending your legs in front of you in a V. With your hands on the floor, lean forward as far as possible. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds.

Row 3 column 4: Thruster. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: 1. Start by doing a front squat 2. At the top position, push the bar above your head (similar to a press) 3. Lower the bar to the shoulders
